I admitted my elder brother to Jagriti Rehabilitation Centre, Taloja Branch, hoping he would receive proper care and support. Unfortunately, on 6th June, we received the shocking news that he had passed away at the age of just 30.
As per the centre, my brother was found unconscious in the washroom around 8:30 AM and was admitted to the hospital around 1:00 PM. However, we still do not know what happened during those crucial hours. Despite repeated attempts by our family and even his treating doctor, Dr. Ayushi, to obtain his medical history and understand the situation, the staff did not respond to calls or provide clear information.
After my brother's death, we requested CCTV footage from the area where he was staying so that we could understand what actually happened. Unfortunately, our requests have been ignored. What has hurt us even more is the rude and insensitive behavior we have faced while seeking answers about our brother's final hours.
We entrusted Jagriti Rehabilitation Centre with my brother's care, believing he would recover and return home safely. Instead, we lost him forever, and we are still left without proper explanations or transparency.

i'm Avinash, a working professional based in Mumbai. I suffered a brain stroke in April 2024, which affected the left side of my body. On my doctor’s recommendation, I began my physiotherapy and rehabilitation journey at Atharva Ability from May to August 2024—and I can confidently say it was one of the correct decision in my recovery journey.

Atharva Ability stands out as one of the best rehabilitation centers, with a team of highly experienced and dedicated physiotherapists. The director, Dr. Gaurish Kenkre, is extremely supportive, calm, and understanding. He takes the time to listen to patients and recommends the most appropriate and effective treatment approach.

When I first started therapy, I was anxious and unsure. However, the positive and encouraging environment at the center helped me feel comfortable and confident. This kind of atmosphere plays a crucial role in a patient’s recovery journey.

My physiotherapist, Dr. Shiwani, played a key role in my progress. She is very experienced, knowledgeable, patient, and attentive. She consistently listened to my concerns and provided tailored exercises to address my challenges.

Even today, she continues to guide me regarding my gym workouts and recovery-related queries. which I truly appreciate.

The entire team at Atharva Ability is extremely caring and vigilant about patient safety. Since many patients have mobility challenges due to stroke, spinal injuries, or other conditions, the staff ensures constant supervision to prevent any accidents.

I would also like to acknowledge the support staff—Mr. Ram, Mr. Srinivas, and Mr. Vicky—for their attentiveness and care.

In addition to Dr. Shiwani, I also received good guidance from Dr. Umair Kazi, Dr. Arpita Shetty, and Dr. Amit Jain. The entire team shares a common goal—ensuring the best possible recovery for their patients.

One moment that truly stands out in my journey was when during a casual chat with Dr. Gaurish i expressed my fear and lack of confidence in walking and balancing. Dr. Gaurish thoughtfully arranged a cricket activity one Sunday and encouraged me to try holding a cricket bat and take a batting stance, ensuring my safety with proper support. That day, I played cricket for the first time after my stroke. It gave me immense confidence and renewed hope for my recovery.

Atharva Ability is among the best robotic rehabilitation centers in BKC, Mumbai, offering advanced equipment, hydrotherapy facilities, and a holistic approach to recovery.

Although my recovery journey is still ongoing, the foundation was built here. Even today, I continue to visit the center for consultations and guidance.

I highly recommend Atharva Ability to anyone recovering from a stroke or injury. Their expertise, infrastructure, and compassionate care truly make a difference.

featured_reviews.name: Rita Varma
featured_reviews.review_text:
I trusted Kibo with my cat, Chittu, for a few days of fluid therapy and oral medication, and it turned out to be one of the worst decisions I’ve made. I had heard good things about them, but my experience was nothing short of traumatic.

Throughout Chittu’s stay, getting updates was incredibly difficult. They only sent pictures after I repeatedly asked, and even those updates didn’t reflect the reality of what my baby was going through. A couple of days later, I noticed bruising in one of the photos, which made me feel something was seriously wrong so I went to pick him up.

What I saw broke me.
My cat had bruises in multiple places, even around the neck. He smelled strongly of urine, as if he had been left lying in it. His fur and skin were in terrible condition, and he was severely dehydrated. The updates they gave me were completely misleading compared to his actual state.

I had provided all his oral medications, yet they were returned to me unopened. This means none of his medications were given, which could have significantly contributed to his decline. His IV catheter wasn’t changed for days, causing phlebitis and bruising at the site, something that no responsible clinic should overlook.

Because of the condition Chittu was in when I brought him home, I was forced to make the heartbreaking decision of putting him to sleep. I cannot express the pain of knowing my baby could have had more time and comfort, but that chance was taken away from him.

Although I understood that my pet’s blood values didn’t indicate a good prognosis, I still believed he deserved every possible chance at recovery. Working in the medical field myself, I’ve seen many patients improve when the right line of treatment is followed. As a pet parent, my only wish was for him to receive proper care, comfort, and hygiene especially towards the end of his life.

Unfortunately, Kibo failed to provide even that basic dignity. What should have been compassionate, attentive care turned into a deeply disappointing and hurtful experience.

I trusted Kibo, and they failed my baby in every possible way. I will never forgive the negligence and lack of basic care that cost my cat his remaining time. I would not recommend this place to anyone who loves their pet.

Edit 23.11 1845 hrs: After our response to the review, you have posted misleading photographs, which we are constrained to clarify - As mentioned below, Chittu was on IV for 9 hours a day. Dear Rita

It is very unfortunate that you had a bad experience with us. We put our heart and soul into the work we do, and your feedback has deeply affected us.

We have an 'open-door' policy for all clients and you did not once raise any of these issues you are now highlighting at any point when Chittu was admitted with us. We would therefore like to clear the air on some of the issues you have raised:

1. Chittu was admitted with us on 29.10.25. His creatine levels were very high and he had totally stopped eating. He was also very dehydrated and was advised renal wet food, which you provided. We used the food you provided.

2. As per the primary vet's prescription (in your case - Crown Vets), we administered slow IV fluid therapy for 9 hours everyday, along with antibiotics and oral medication. We used the medicines available in our existing inventory (since these were already opened), and therefore did not use the fresh batch of the drugs you provided, which was duly returned to you unused and unopened.

3. Pursuant to the treatment administered, Chittu began eating slowly (chicken liver) and showed some signs of improvement. We gave you regular and daily updates on WhatsApp with pictures, status of his food intake etc. After your review, we have also forwarded screenshots of all updates to your WhatsApp number again.

4. However, on 08.11.25 (9th day at Kibo), Chittu was looking dull and had stopped eating. We promptly informed you, and you came and took him from the centre to get him checked with the primary vet. Chittu was cleaned, put in a clean basket and handed over to you. Pictures of the cat were also shared with you as per our protocol. There was no bruising whatsoever, and it is completely not true that you came to pick up Chittu because of bruising, that is simply not true.

5. Less than 2 hours later, you informed us that Chittu was no more. You also informed us that you come the following day to pick up the unused medicines which you would use for your other rescues/ community cats.

At the time we handed the cat over to you, Chittu was not discharged from Kibo and you took him for a checkup since his condition was deteriorating. It is therefore quite shocking to note your feedback, which is completely contrary to what has transpired. Chittu certainly deserved every chance of recovery and we have provided him that to the best of the medical advice given by the primary vet.

We are all part of the community working for the betterment of animals. We are all human, and to err is human. At Kibo, we have a strong policy of admitting that we have made a mistake if that were the case. Because from that mistake comes a much bigger learning. But this is simply not the case here, it is very unfortunate you have this feedback. 

We have also tried contacting you multiple times but have not been able to get through. We remain available to discuss anything further on this should you require.

Regards
Team Kibo

featured_reviews.name: foram chheda
featured_reviews.review_text:
After my doctor recommended Miran Physio Centre for my back pain, I decided to give it a try and I’m truly glad I did. Due to long hours of desk work, my posture had significantly deteriorated, which was contributing to persistent discomfort.

At Miran, not only did I correct my posture, but I also built considerable strength and body awareness along the way.

Dr. Dhvani is extremely attentive and thorough. She consistently monitored my progress and thoughtfully modified my exercises based on my health condition and recovery stage. What really stood out was her depth of understanding as a neuro-physiotherapist — she identifies the root cause of the problem in a much deeper way rather than just treating the symptoms. She doesn’t just focus on your current pain but also guides you on long-term corrective strategies and sustainable workouts that benefit you in the long run.
Her team deserves special appreciation as well. They are exceptionally well-trained, supportive, and create a warm, encouraging environment — more like friends who genuinely care about your recovery.
Miran is not just a physiotherapy centre; it is truly a space dedicated to overall wellness and long-term health.
